Governance review

Board rules and contract control

The board received upgrade control over two contracts, but several internal permissions remained unchanged. The records below separate those powers and examine the board’s approval and veto rules.

Board approval rules

The four-seat board requires three YES votes. That means any three can approve an action over the fourth seat’s objection or absence. A159, A249 and A271 show why beneficiary disclosure and recusal matter across the whole board.

A272 proposed removing Vini and reducing the threshold to 60%. It failed: 0xphilipp and MB voted YES, Rose voted NO and Vini was absent. The current captured board remains four seats at 75%. Sequence alone does not establish motive.

The Think Tank cast no YES or NO votes on four veto proposals

Four substantive veto proposals had zero YES and zero NO ballots. Only limited abstentions were recorded. The technical member proposed all five and abstained on all five. P5’s empty message means the proposed veto could not execute even if approved.

The records leave two problems to resolve: missing votes and an empty veto message. Membership history, notifications and proposal construction need checking; the reasons for non-participation are unknown.

Original handover commitments

The 2024 TLA launch text says registry ownership transfers after three months and contract admin after one month. The packaged ledger identifies 31 privileged operations in 19 transactions after its conservative cutoff, affecting seven original contracts. The original commitment and current roles were independently checked; every historical ledger operation was not replayed in this review.

Successful transactions prove use of an address’s authority, not exclusive human key custody. No approved extension was found in the reviewed records; an agreement elsewhere remains possible.

  1. 9 Oct · 03:09:55 UTC

    Seven redelegations totalled 1,680,127.496132 LUNA, including 662,828.893153 LUNA away from Ceres.

Compare the eligibility criteria, whitelist, gauge outputs and public rationale immediately before and after the change. These hub staking redelegations are distinct from Phoenix Alliance allocations. Timing alone does not establish retaliation, favoritism or coordinated voting.

Other retained permissions

The 27 October queries show the published ERIS configuration address as hub and prop-gauge owner, while the hub’s raw vote operator points to the prop-gauge. Creda’s registry identifies the protocol fee account as reserve controller; the Portfolio’s migration administrator is a separate role.

The successful FEE_COLLECTOR assignment, Treasury configuration-role assignment and arbLUNA collateral addition also document uses of retained authority. These records show assigned permissions and asset movements; they do not establish personal profit. Two Creda reserve collections included 5,701.254836 and 2,679.750683 LUNA, alongside other assets that remain separately denominated.

These current responses do not establish the requested historical snapshots: providers did not return headers confirming those heights. Match permissions to deployed code before asserting every supported capability, and do not infer exclusive personal key custody from a public role label.

  • Authority events, current roles and reserve collections
  • Raw hub vote-operator response
  • Creda reserve-controller roles

Why ERIS says it made source code private

ERIS’s retrospective says appropriate contracts were moved to private source for security. That is ERIS’s explanation for the missing public source.

The stated rationale does not independently establish stronger security or audit coverage for every deployed 2026 revision. Public audit reports exist; independent review still needs the auditor, scope, source commit, deployed checksum, outstanding findings and remediation.

  • ERIS explanation and security claims
  • Published ERIS audit reports
  • Scope of the transaction checks

Longer-term reforms

Disclose and recuse

Maintain a current stakeholder register covering grants, compensation, OTC, hosting, delegations and voting power. Require recusal and independent approval for related-party decisions, with the rationale published.

Make veto proposals usable

Give the Think Tank reliable notifications, complete executable messages, adequate voting windows and published rationales. Publish participation records and investigate failed veto proposals.

Separate technical powers

Document migration admin, internal owner, treasury control and vote operator separately. Use explicit acceptance for ownership transfers, independent verification and runbooks for emergency action.

Publish voting instructions and results

Publish hub/gauge intentions and final ballots, validator-mandate rules and material voting-power holders at entity level. Preserve weighted dissent and avoid interpreting delegation as ownership.

Record each payment’s approval and acceptance

Keep the budget, recipient, declared conflicts, promised work, acceptance, entitlement, claim and valuation together. Independently reconcile recurring expenses and related-party OTC execution.

Review and respond

Commission periodic independent control review with access to off-chain agreements. Give affected stakeholders a right of response and publish corrections against specific evidence.
